questions.question: Q1. What happens to the vertical tire load ($F_z$) of the inside wheel during a sharp turn?

answers.a: It increases due to aerodynamic downforce
answers.b: It remains equal to the nominal static weight of 1200 N
answers.c: It decreases because lateral load transfer shifts weight to the outside wheel
answers.d: It drops instantly to zero regardless of steering angle

explanations.a: Incorrect. Aerodynamic downforce is not modeled here; the load change is driven by lateral mechanics.
explanations.b: Incorrect. The weight stays at 1200 N only when driving straight with a 0-degree steering angle.
explanations.c: Correct. Lateral load transfer ($\Delta F_z$) subtracts vertical load from the inner wheel and adds it to the outer wheel during cornering.
explanations.d: Incorrect. The weight decrease is proportional to the steering angle, not an instantaneous drop to zero.

questions.question: Q2. Under a rigid 50:50 power split drivetrain configuration, why does an EV tend to spin out during high-torque cornering?

answers.a: The outside tire receives more torque than it can physically handle
answers.b: The inner tire's force demand exceeds its reduced traction limit ceiling due to weight transfer
answers.c: The steering angle locks up automatically because of high motor currents
answers.d: Surface friction coefficients dynamically increase on the inner side of the track

explanations.a: Incorrect. Under a 50:50 split, both rear tires receive an identical torque demand.
explanations.b: Correct. Weight transfer starves the inner wheel of vertical load, lowering its traction ceiling ($F_{\text{limit}}$). Because the rigid split forces it to maintain equal torque demand, $F_{\text{demand}} > F_{\text{limit}}$, triggering slip.
explanations.c: Incorrect. The steering system remains active, but mechanical traction is lost at the tire patch.
explanations.d: Incorrect. The surface friction coefficient ($\mu$) is an environmental constant determined by the road surface.

questions.question: Q3. How does the Intelligent Torque Vectoring system stabilize the vehicle when tire slip is detected?

answers.a: By increasing torque equally across all four wheels to push through the skid
answers.b: By adjusting the surface friction coefficient ($\mu$) of the concrete track
answers.c: By dynamically cutting or reallocating torque at the wheel exceeding its grip ceiling to match its traction limits
answers.d: By locking the steering angle to 0 degrees until the vehicle stops

explanations.a: Incorrect. Adding equal power would worsen the slip condition on the overloaded tire patch.
explanations.b: Incorrect. A vehicle control system cannot change physical environmental road properties like road friction.
explanations.c: Correct. The controller limits the torque on the grip-starved wheel to ensure that tire force demand does not exceed the available traction limit ceiling ($F_{\text{demand}} \le F_{\text{limit}}$).
explanations.d: Incorrect. The driver maintains control over steering, while the software manages powertrain distribution.

questions.question: Q4. According to the physics model used in this simulation, what parameters determine the Traction Limit Ceiling ($F_{\text{limit}}$) of a tire?

answers.a: Base motor torque and tire rolling radius
answers.b: Surface friction coefficient ($\mu$) and instantaneous vertical tire load ($F_z$)
answers.c: Steering angle scaling factor and yaw velocity
answers.d: Chassis body roll angle and timer duration

explanations.a: Incorrect. Torque and radius determine the tire force demand ($F_{\text{demand}}$), not the maximum grip ceiling.
explanations.b: Correct. The simulation calculates the maximum sustainable traction using the formula $F_{\text{limit}} = \mu \times F_z$.
explanations.c: Incorrect. Steering scaling influences the longitudinal force demand penalty during turning, not traction capacity.
explanations.d: Incorrect. Body roll and time are telemetry outputs, not factors that define raw frictional tire ceiling limits.

questions.question: Q5. What physical parameter dictates the empirical steering penalty correction factor ($f_{\text{steer}}$) inside the force demand calculations?

answers.c: The absolute value of the vehicle's steering angle
answers.d: The base weight component of 1200 N

explanations.a: Incorrect. Surface friction operates independently from the steering geometry algorithm.
explanations.b: Incorrect. The scaling factor is a kinematic variable and has no relationship with the clock.
explanations.c: Correct. The steering scale factor is calculated live as $1 + |\text{steeringAngle}| \times 0.02$, which scales force demand based on turning severity.
explanations.d: Incorrect. The vertical static load component is used to calculate grip thresholds, not steering geometric scaling.
